exposure: Implementation of an evidence-based induction of labor (IOL) guideline
Utilization of evidence-based IOL practices (combined agent ripening, vaginal misoprostol, early amniotomy)
cohort: 495 birthing people with singleton pregnancies, intact membranes, and cervical dilation <=2 cm admitted for induction of labor.
finding: Implementation of an evidence-based induction of labor guideline was associated with shorter IOL length and faster time to delivery.
mod_finding: No significant difference in cesarean delivery rates was observed after guideline implementation.
cross-section timing: Pre-implementation period: November 1, 2021 through January 31, 2022; Post-implementation period: March 1, 2022 through April 30, 2022
